lanes.label: The Word and the first signs
Signs and the bread of life
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.t: The Word Became Flesh
nodes.d: John opens with the Word, who was in the beginning with God and was God, through whom all things were made, who is life and light, and who became flesh and dwelt among us full of grace and truth; John the Baptist is sent to witness to the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John 1 teaches about who the Word is and what he did?
ev: Say what John says about the Word before creation, in creation and in becoming flesh.

nodes.t: John the Baptist's Witness
nodes.d: Priests and Levites ask John who he is; he says he is not the Christ but a voice crying in the wilderness, and next day he sees Jesus and calls him the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world and the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how John described himself and what he called Jesus?
ev: Say who John said he was and what he called Jesus.

nodes.t: The First Disciples
nodes.d: Andrew and another follow Jesus, Andrew brings Simon who is named Cephas, Philip finds Nathanael, who confesses Jesus the Son of God and King of Israel, and Jesus says they will see angels ascending and descending on the Son of man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the first disciples Jesus gathered and what Nathanael said about him?
ev: Name the first disciples called and what Nathanael confessed.

nodes.t: Water Made Wine at Cana
nodes.d: At a wedding in Cana of Galilee the wine runs out; Jesus has the stone waterpots filled and the water becomes wine, which John calls the beginning of his signs, manifesting his glory so that his disciples believed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the water becoming wine and what it revealed?
ev: Retell the miracle and what John says it showed.

nodes.t: Jesus Cleanses the Temple
nodes.d: At Passover Jesus drives the sellers and money-changers out of the temple; asked for a sign, he says 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up', which John says he spoke of the temple of his body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he meant by raising the temple in three days?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what sign he named and what John says it meant.

nodes.t: Born Again: Nicodemus
nodes.d: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night and is told that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit; Jesus compares the Spirit to wind and says the Son of man must be lifted up like the serpent Moses lifted so that believers have eternal life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Nicodemus about being born again?
ev: Say what Jesus told Nicodemus about new birth and being lifted up.

nodes.t: God So Loved the World
nodes.d: The discourse continues: God gave his only begotten Son so that whoever believes should not perish but have eternal life; the Son came not to condemn but to save, and men loved darkness rather than light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John 3:16-21 says about God's love, belief and the light?
ev: Say what God gave, who receives life, and why people reject the light.

nodes.t: John: He Must Increase
nodes.d: John the Baptist, still baptizing, is told that Jesus baptizes and many come; he says he is only the bridegroom's friend and that Jesus must increase while he decreases, because the one who comes from above is above all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain John the Baptist's words about Jesus increasing?
ev: Say how John responds to Jesus' growing following and what he says about the Son.

nodes.t: The Woman at the Well
nodes.d: At Jacob's well in Samaria, Jesus asks a woman for water, offers living water, shows he knows her life, and tells her that true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and truth, and when she speaks of Messiah he says he is he.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus offered the Samaritan woman and what he taught about worship?
ev: Say what Jesus offered the woman and what he said about worship.

nodes.t: The Harvest in Samaria
nodes.d: The woman tells the town, Jesus tells his disciples that his food is to do the will of him who sent him and to finish his work, and many Samaritans believe, some because of the woman and more because they heard him themselves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words about food and the harvest and how Samaritans believed?
ev: Say what Jesus said was his food and how the Samaritans came to believe.

nodes.t: The Nobleman's Son Healed
nodes.d: A nobleman at Cana asks Jesus to come heal his dying son; Jesus says 'Thy son liveth', the man believes and finds his son recovered at the same hour, and John calls this the second sign in Galilee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the nobleman's son?
ev: Say what Jesus said, how the father acted and what he learned.

nodes.t: Healing at Bethesda on the Sabbath
nodes.d: At a feast in Jerusalem Jesus heals a man who had been ill thirty-eight years by the pool of Bethesda and tells him to take up his bed; because it is the sabbath the Jews persecute Jesus, and when he says his Father works they seek to kill him for making himself equal with God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing at Bethesda and why the Jews opposed Jesus?
ev: Say what Jesus did and why the leaders wanted to kill him.

nodes.t: The Son's Work and Authority
nodes.d: Jesus says the Son does only what he sees the Father do, gives life as the Father does, has been given all judgment, and that those who hear his word and believe have eternal life; the dead will hear his voice and come out of the graves to life or judgment.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the Son's work, life and judgment?
ev: Say what Jesus says the Son does with the Father and what he says about life and judgment.

nodes.t: Witnesses to Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus names the witnesses to him: John, his works, the Father, and the Scriptures, which testify of him, and says Moses wrote of him and accuses those who will not come to him for life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the witnesses Jesus gives for himself and what he says about Moses?
ev: List the witnesses Jesus names and what he says about Moses.

nodes.t: The Feeding of the Five Thousand
nodes.d: Near Passover a large crowd follows Jesus; he tests Philip, takes a boy's five barley loaves and two fishes, gives thanks and distributes, all are filled and twelve baskets are gathered; the people want to take him by force to make him king.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand in John 6?
ev: Retell the miracle and what the crowd wanted to do after.

nodes.t: Jesus Walks on the Sea
nodes.d: At night, with a wind blowing, the disciples row across the sea and see Jesus walking on the water; he says 'It is I; be not afraid', and the boat is immediately at land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus walking on the sea?
ev: Say what the disciples saw and what Jesus said.

nodes.t: I Am the Bread of Life
nodes.d: The crowd seeks Jesus for the loaves; he says to labour for food that endures, that believing is the work of God, that Moses did not give the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life; all the Father gives him will come and he will raise them at the last day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by 'I am the bread of life' in this passage?
ev: Say what Jesus says he is and what he promises those who come to him.

nodes.t: Eat My Flesh, Drink My Blood
nodes.d: The Jews murmur that Jesus said he came down from heaven; he says no man comes unless the Father draws him, and that unless they eat his flesh and drink his blood they have no life; he contrasts himself with the manna their fathers ate.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says in John 6 about the Father drawing and about eating his flesh?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the Father's drawing and about eating his flesh and drinking his blood.

nodes.t: Many Disciples Turn Back; Peter's Confession
nodes.d: Many disciples find the teaching hard and leave; Jesus asks the twelve if they will go too, and Peter answers 'to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life' and confesses him as the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus says one of them is a devil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why many disciples left and what Peter confessed?
ev: Say why many left and what Peter said.

nodes.t: Jesus and His Brothers: Going Up to the Feast
nodes.d: Near the feast of tabernacles, Jesus' brothers, who do not believe in him, tell him to show himself in Judaea; he says his time has not come and goes up later privately, while people murmur about him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened between Jesus and his brothers before the feast of tabernacles?
ev: Say what his brothers said, what he answered, and how the people reacted.

nodes.t: Teaching in the Temple at the Feast
nodes.d: In the middle of the feast Jesus teaches in the temple, saying his doctrine is from the one who sent him; he answers the charge about healing on the sabbath, the crowd debates whether he is the Christ, and officers sent to seize him do not.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus claimed about his teaching and how people responded?
ev: Say where Jesus said his doctrine came from and how the crowd divided.

nodes.t: Rivers of Living Water
nodes.d: On the last great day of the feast Jesus cries out that anyone who thirsts should come to him and drink and rivers of living water will flow from the believer, which John says refers to the Spirit to be given after Jesus is glorified; the crowd, officers and Pharisees divide, and Nicodemus speaks for a fair hearing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus offered on the last day of the feast and what John says it means?
ev: Say what Jesus invited people to do and what John says the living water means.

nodes.t: The Woman Taken in Adultery
nodes.d: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman caught in adultery to Jesus to test him; he says the one without sin may cast the first stone, they leave one by one, and Jesus tells her he does not condemn her and to go and sin no more.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the woman taken in adultery and what Jesus said?
ev: Say what Jesus said to the accusers and to the woman.

nodes.t: I Am the Light of the World
nodes.d: Jesus says 'I am the light of the world', that whoever follows him will not walk in darkness, and defends his testimony as true because the Father who sent him also bears witness; he says those who do not believe that he is he will die in their sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain 'I am the light of the world' and what Jesus warns those who do not believe?
ev: Say what Jesus says about himself as light and what he says to those who do not believe.

nodes.t: The Truth Will Set You Free
nodes.d: To Jews who believed him, Jesus says continuing in his word means being his disciples and knowing the truth that makes free; he says whoever commits sin is sin's servant, and the Son sets free indeed, and denies that those seeking to kill him are doing Abraham's works.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus means by the truth making free and who he says is a servant of sin?
ev: Say what Jesus says sets people free and what he says about who is a servant of sin.

nodes.t: Before Abraham Was, I Am
nodes.d: The Jews accuse Jesus of a devil; he says Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and when they say he is not fifty and has seen Abraham, Jesus says 'Before Abraham was, I am', and they take up stones.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about Abraham and how his hearers responded?
ev: Say what Jesus said about Abraham and how the Jews reacted.

nodes.t: A Man Born Blind Is Healed
nodes.d: Jesus sees a man blind from birth, says the blindness is so God's works may be shown, declares himself the light of the world, anoints his eyes with clay and sends him to wash in Siloam, and the man sees.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus healed the man born blind?
ev: Say why the man was blind according to Jesus and how he was healed.

nodes.t: The Healed Man Before the Pharisees
nodes.d: The Pharisees question the healed man and his parents, divide over the sabbath, and cast the man out when he says Jesus must be from God; Jesus finds him, the man believes and worships, and Jesus says those who say 'we see' remain in sin.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened when the healed man was questioned and what Jesus said to him afterwards?
ev: Say how the healed man answered the Pharisees and what happened when Jesus found him.

nodes.t: I Am the Door and the Good Shepherd
nodes.d: Jesus says he is the door of the sheep and the good shepherd who knows his sheep, lays down his life for them, has other sheep not of this fold, and has power to lay down his life and take it again.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the good shepherd teaching and what it says about Jesus' life and death?
ev: Say what Jesus says the good shepherd does and what he says about his life.

nodes.t: I and My Father Are One
nodes.d: At the feast of dedication the Jews ask Jesus to say plainly if he is the Christ; he says his sheep hear his voice and no one can pluck them from his hand and 'I and my Father are one', and they take up stones, but he escapes beyond Jordan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about his sheep and his oneness with the Father?
ev: Say what Jesus says about his sheep and about himself and the Father.

nodes.t: Lazarus Is Sick and Dies
nodes.d: Mary and Martha send word that Lazarus is sick; Jesus says the sickness is for the glory of God, stays two days, then tells the disciples Lazarus sleeps and is dead, and Thomas says they may go and die with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus said about Lazarus's illness and why he waited?
ev: Say what Jesus said about Lazarus's sickness and what he did.

nodes.t: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
nodes.d: Martha meets Jesus, who tells her that her brother will rise again and says 'I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live'; Martha confesses him the Christ, the Son of God, and Mary and the mourners weep and Jesus weeps.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says to Martha about the resurrection and life?
ev: Say what Jesus said to Martha and what she answered.

nodes.t: Jesus Raises Lazarus
nodes.d: At the tomb Jesus has the stone taken away, prays to the Father, and cries 'Lazarus, come forth'; the dead man comes out bound in graveclothes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the raising of Lazarus?
ev: Retell the raising of Lazarus.

nodes.t: The Council Plots to Kill Jesus
nodes.d: Many believe after the raising of Lazarus, but others tell the Pharisees; the chief priests and Pharisees hold a council, and Caiaphas says one man should die for the people, which John says was prophecy, and from that day they plan to put Jesus to death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the council plotted against Jesus and what Caiaphas said?
ev: Say what the council feared, what Caiaphas said and what John says it meant.

nodes.t: Mary Anoints Jesus at Bethany
nodes.d: Six days before Passover a supper is made at Bethany; Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly ointment, Judas objects but John says he was a thief, and Jesus says she kept it for the day of his burying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Mary's anointing of Jesus and Judas's objection?
ev: Say what Mary did, what Judas said and how Jesus answered.

nodes.t: The Entry into Jerusalem
nodes.d: The crowd takes palm branches and cries 'Hosanna', Jesus rides a young donkey as written, the disciples later remember this after he is glorified, and the Pharisees say the world has gone after him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' entry into Jerusalem in John?
ev: Say how the crowd greeted Jesus and what John says the disciples understood later.

nodes.t: The Hour Has Come: A Grain of Wheat
nodes.d: Greeks ask to see Jesus; he says the hour has come for the Son of man to be glorified, that a grain of wheat must fall and die to bear fruit, that when he is lifted up he will draw all men, and a voice from heaven answers his prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the grain of wheat saying and what Jesus says about being lifted up?
ev: Say what Jesus says about the grain of wheat and about being lifted up.

nodes.t: Unbelief and Jesus' Final Public Words
nodes.d: Despite many signs the people do not believe, which John says fulfils Isaiah, and many rulers believe but fear confessing him; Jesus cries that believing in him is believing in the one who sent him and that he came as light, not to judge but to save.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what John says about unbelief and what Jesus says about his words and judgment?
ev: Say why John says the people did not believe and what Jesus says about those who hear and reject his words.

nodes.t: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
nodes.d: Before the Passover, knowing his hour has come, Jesus rises from supper and washes his disciples' feet; he says Peter will know later and that those he washes are clean, then tells them to wash one another's feet as he did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the foot washing and what Jesus said it was for?
ev: Say what Jesus did, what Peter said and what Jesus told the disciples to do.

nodes.t: Jesus Identifies the Betrayer
nodes.d: Troubled in spirit, Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him; he gives a sop to Judas, Satan enters Judas, Jesus tells him to do quickly what he does, and Judas goes out into the night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Judas was identified and what he did?
ev: Say how Jesus pointed to the betrayer and what Judas did.

nodes.t: A New Commandment
nodes.d: After Judas leaves, Jesus says the Son of man is now glorified and gives a new commandment to love one another as he loved them, by which all men will know they are his disciples; he tells Peter he will deny him thrice before the cock crows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus' new commandment is and what he foretold about Peter?
ev: Say what the new commandment is and what Jesus told Peter.

nodes.t: I Am the Way, the Truth and the Life
nodes.d: Jesus tells the disciples not to be troubled, that he goes to prepare a place in his Father's house and will come again; to Thomas he says 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me', and to Philip that seeing him is seeing the Father.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says about the way to the Father and the place he prepares?
ev: Say what Jesus promised about the Father's house and what he said about the way to the Father.

nodes.t: The Promise of the Comforter
nodes.d: Jesus promises to ask the Father to give another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, who will abide with them and teach and remind them of all he said; he leaves his peace and says that those who love him keep his word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus promises about the Comforter and the Holy Ghost in John 14?
ev: Say what Jesus promises about the Spirit and what he says about loving him.

nodes.t: I Am the True Vine
nodes.d: Jesus says he is the true vine, the Father the husbandman and the disciples the branches; they must abide in him to bear fruit, keep his commandments, love one another, and are called friends whom he chose.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the vine and branches picture and what abiding means?
ev: Say what Jesus says branches must do and what he says about love and friends.

nodes.t: The World's Hatred and the Witness of the Spirit
nodes.d: Jesus warns the disciples that the world hated him first and will hate them and persecute them, that the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, will testify of him, and that they will also bear witness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the world hates the disciples and who will bear witness according to Jesus?
ev: Say why Jesus says the world will hate his disciples and who will testify.

nodes.t: The Work of the Spirit
nodes.d: Jesus says it is expedient that he goes away so the Comforter will come, who will reprove the world of sin, righteousness and judgment, guide the disciples into all truth and glorify Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus says the Spirit will do for the world and for the disciples?
ev: Say what the Spirit will do when he comes.

nodes.t: Sorrow Turned to Joy; I Have Overcome the World
nodes.d: Jesus says the disciples will weep but their sorrow will become joy, like a woman after travail, promises that the Father will give what they ask in his name, and says that though they will be scattered he has overcome the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus' words on sorrow turning to joy and 'I have overcome the world'?
ev: Say what Jesus says about their sorrow and his last words about peace and the world.

nodes.t: Jesus' Prayer for Glory and for His Disciples
nodes.d: Jesus looks to heaven and prays for the Father to glorify the Son, says eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, and prays for the disciples he has kept, that the Father would keep them, sanctify them by truth, and not take them out of the world.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus prays for himself and his disciples in John 17?
ev: Say what Jesus asks for himself and for the disciples.

nodes.t: Jesus' Prayer for All Believers
nodes.d: Jesus prays for those who will believe through the disciples' word, that they may all be one as the Father is in him and he in the Father so the world may believe, and that they be with him to see his glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jesus prays for in John 17:20-26 and what he asks?
ev: Say who Jesus prays for here and what he asks.

nodes.t: Jesus Is Arrested in the Garden
nodes.d: Jesus crosses the brook Cedron to a garden; Judas comes with soldiers and officers, Jesus says 'I am he' and they fall backward, he asks that his disciples go free, rebukes Peter's sword-cutting and says he must drink the cup the Father gave him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the arrest of Jesus in John 18?
ev: Say what happened when Jesus said 'I am he' and what he told Peter.

nodes.t: Before Annas; Peter Denies
nodes.d: Jesus is taken to Annas and Caiaphas and is questioned about his disciples and doctrine; meanwhile Peter at the fire three times denies being his disciple, and a cock crows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus before the high priest and Peter's denials?
ev: Say what Jesus said to the high priest and what Peter did.

nodes.t: Jesus Before Pilate: My Kingdom Is Not of This World
nodes.d: The Jews take Jesus to Pilate; Pilate asks if he is King of the Jews, Jesus says his kingdom is not of this world and that he came to bear witness to the truth, Pilate finds no fault, and the crowd asks for Barabbas.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom?
ev: Say what Jesus told Pilate about his kingdom and who the crowd chose.

nodes.t: Scourged, Mocked and Sentenced
nodes.d: Pilate has Jesus scourged and mocked with a crown of thorns; the Jews say he made himself the Son of God and, when Pilate seeks to release him, cry 'Crucify him' and say 'We have no king but Caesar'; Pilate delivers Jesus to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified?
ev: Say what the soldiers did, what the Jews cried and what Pilate finally did.

nodes.t: The Crucifixion
nodes.d: Jesus carries his cross to Golgotha and is crucified between two others under a title 'Jesus of Nazareth the King of the Jews'; soldiers cast lots for his coat, he commits his mother to the beloved disciple, says 'I thirst' and 'It is finished', bows his head and gives up the ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the crucifixion in John and name Jesus' last words?
ev: Say what Jesus said from the cross and what the soldiers did with his clothes.

nodes.t: His Side Pierced and the Burial
nodes.d: The soldiers do not break Jesus' legs but pierce his side, and John says these things fulfil Scripture; Joseph of Arimathaea and Nicodemus wrap his body with spices and lay it in a new tomb in a garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what happened to Jesus' body after his death and who buried him?
ev: Say what the soldiers did and who buried Jesus.

nodes.t: The Empty Tomb
nodes.d: Mary Magdalene finds the stone taken away and tells Peter and the beloved disciple; they run to the tomb, find the linen clothes lying, and the other disciple sees and believes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Peter and the other disciple found at the tomb?
ev: Say what the disciples found in the tomb.

nodes.t: Jesus Appears to Mary Magdalene
nodes.d: Mary weeps at the tomb, sees two angels, turns and takes Jesus for the gardener until he says her name; she tells the disciples she has seen the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Mary Magdalene met the risen Jesus?
ev: Say how Mary recognised Jesus and what she told the disciples.

nodes.t: Jesus Appears to the Disciples
nodes.d: On the evening of the first day Jesus stands among the disciples behind shut doors, shows his hands and side, says 'Peace be unto you', sends them as the Father sent him, breathes on them and says 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost'.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jesus showed and told the disciples on the evening of the resurrection?
ev: Say what Jesus showed them and what he told them.

nodes.t: Thomas and the Purpose of John's Book
nodes.d: Thomas, absent the first time, says he will not believe unless he sees and touches; eight days later Jesus appears and Thomas says 'My Lord and my God'; John says the signs are written that readers may believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of Thomas and say why John says he wrote?
ev: Say what Thomas said and why John says the book was written.

nodes.t: The Great Catch and Breakfast by the Sea
nodes.d: Seven disciples fish all night without a catch; Jesus on the shore tells them to cast on the right side and the net is full, the beloved disciple says 'It is the Lord', Peter swims ashore, and Jesus gives them bread and fish by a fire of coals.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Jesus' appearance by the sea of Tiberias?
ev: Retell the catch and how the disciples recognised Jesus.

nodes.t: Peter Restored and the Last Words
nodes.d: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him and tells him to feed his sheep, foretells how Peter will die, tells him to follow him and not worry about the beloved disciple; John says this disciple wrote these things and that the world could not hold all that Jesus did.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Jesus asked Peter and told him after breakfast?
ev: Say what Jesus asked Peter and told him to do.

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: God creates the world
nodes.d: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?
ev: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it

nodes.t: Jacob's dream at Bethel
nodes.d: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven, and the LORD renews the promise to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Jacob's dream and what God promised?
ev: Retell the dream
State the promise in 28:13-15

nodes.t: Rules for keeping the Passover
nodes.d: The ordinance of the Passover is set out: no foreigner or hired servant may eat of it, a bought servant who is circumcised may, the lamb is eaten in one house and no bone of it broken, and a sojourner who wants to keep it must be circumcised. One law covers native and stranger.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the Passover rules say about foreigners and about the lamb's bones?
ev: Say what is required of a stranger who wants to keep the Passover (12:48)
Say what was not to be done with the lamb's bones (12:46)

nodes.t: Bread from heaven: manna and quails
nodes.d: Israel murmurs for the food of Egypt. The LORD sends quails in the evening and manna in the morning, a day's portion to be gathered daily, with a double portion on the sixth day for the sabbath. An omer of manna is kept before the Testimony.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the manna was gathered each day and what was different on the sixth and seventh days?
ev: Say what the people were to do each day and on the sixth day (16:4-5, 16:22-26)
Say what happened to manna kept overnight against the command (16:19-20)
Say how long Israel ate manna (16:35)

nodes.t: Numbers: overview
nodes.d: Numbers follows Israel from Sinai through the wilderness: the census, camp and Levites, departure from Sinai, the rebellion at Kadesh and forty years of wandering, Balaam, a second census, and preparation on the plains of Moab for entering the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of where Israel starts and ends in Numbers?
ev: Describe the journey in Numbers in three stages: at Sinai, wandering, and on the plains of Moab.

nodes.t: The fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
nodes.d: Numbers 21:4-9 tells how the people speak against God and Moses, the LORD sends fiery serpents, the people confess, and Moses makes a bronze serpent on a pole so that anyone bitten who looks at it lives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the story of the bronze serpent and say what the people had to do to live?
ev: Say what the people said, what the LORD sent, and how those bitten were healed.

nodes.t: Cities of refuge and honest witnesses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 19 commands three cities of refuge in the land for accidental killers while the murderer who lies in wait is to be handed over, forbids moving a neighbour's landmark, and requires two or three witnesses, with the penalty of the false witness being what he intended for his brother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why a false witness received the punishment he planned for another?
ev: Say how an accidental killing differs from murder in this chapter.
Say what happens to a false witness (19:16-21).

nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 22: my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
nodes.d: The speaker cries to God who seems far, is scorned and surrounded by enemies, his bones out of joint and garments divided, then declares God’s name in the congregation and says all the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 22 moves from the opening cry to the closing praise?
ev: Read 22:1-21 and list the pictures of suffering.
Read 22:22-31 and say how the psalm ends.

nodes.t: Psalm 41: blessed is he that considers the poor
nodes.d: The one who considers the poor is blessed and the LORD delivers him in trouble; the speaker, ill and slandered by enemies and even a familiar friend, asks for mercy and the psalm ends with a blessing on the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what blessing Psalm 41:1-3 gives to the one who considers the poor?
ev: Read 41:1-3 and 41:9-13 and say who is blessed and who betrays the speaker.

nodes.t: Psalm 69: zeal for thy house; they gave me vinegar
nodes.d: The speaker is sinking in deep waters and hated without cause, says zeal for God’s house has consumed him and reproaches have fallen on him, that he was given gall and vinegar, asks that his adversaries’ table be a snare and their eyes darkened, and ends with praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the suffering in Psalm 69:1-4 and 69:20-21 and how the psalm ends?
ev: Read 69:1-4, 69:9, 69:21 and 69:22-28 and list what the speaker suffers and asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 78: tell the coming generation what God did and how Israel rebelled
nodes.d: The speaker says the fathers must teach their children the LORD’s works so they will not be stubborn like their fathers; he retells Egypt, the sea, the wilderness provision and Israel’s repeated unbelief, God’s anger, and his choosing of Judah, Zion and David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the psalmist retells Israel’s history in Psalm 78:1-8 and what repeated pattern follows?
ev: Read 78:1-8 and say why the story is told.
Trace the cycle of provision, rebellion and judgment in 78:12-64.

nodes.t: Psalms 81-82: hear my people; God judges among the gods
nodes.d: Psalm 81 calls Israel to sing and recalls the LORD who brought them from Egypt, who asks them to listen and says he would have fed them had they obeyed; Psalm 82 shows God standing in the congregation to judge those who judge unjustly and favour the wicked.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God says in Psalm 81:8-13 and what he says to the judges in Psalm 82:2-4?
ev: Read 81:8-16 and 82:1-4 and say what God asks and rebukes.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Isaiah sees the Lord and is sent
nodes.d: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the LORD enthroned with seraphim crying holy, is cleansed by a coal from the altar, volunteers, and is told to preach to a people who will not understand until a stump remains.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Isaiah's vision in chapter 6, including what the seraphim cry and how Isaiah is cleansed?
ev: Retell what the seraphim say and do (6:2-7)
Explain Isaiah's response in 6:5 and 6:8
Describe the message he is given and the "holy seed" in 6:9-13

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Sing, barren one: the covenant of peace
nodes.d: The barren woman is told to sing and enlarge her tent, the LORD her husband has called her back with mercy, swears as with the waters of Noah, and promises a covenant of peace that will not be removed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD compares his promise in Isaiah 54:9-10 to the waters of Noah?
ev: Describe the call to the barren woman (54:1-3)
Say what the LORD compares his oath to (54:9)
Quote the promise in 54:10

nodes.t: Zechariah: overview
nodes.d: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?
ev: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)

nodes.t: Thy King cometh, lowly and riding on an ass
nodes.d: A burden against Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre and Philistia is followed by a call for Zion to rejoice because her just and saving King comes lowly on an ass; he cuts off chariot and bow, speaks peace to the nations, and the LORD saves his people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the King of Zechariah 9:9-10 and what he does?
ev: Say what is said of the King in 9:9
Describe his rule in 9:10
Read the promise to prisoners in 9:11-12

nodes.t: Jerusalem a burdensome stone; they look on the pierced
nodes.d: The LORD will make Jerusalem a cup of trembling and a burdensome stone to the nations that gather against her, and will pour on David's house and Jerusalem the spirit of grace and supplications, so that they look on him whom they have pierced and mourn.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Zechariah 12:10 says the LORD will pour out and what the people do?
ev: Describe what happens to nations that attack Jerusalem (12:2-3, 12:9)
Read 12:10 and describe the mourning that follows (12:10-14)
